A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UserMirrorer. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and some relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original user-simulation accuracy, downstream recommendation experiments, data-selection comparisons and feature ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds proprietary-model comparisons, prediction-entropy analysis, reasoning-style measurements and cross-domain experiments.

M1.justification: Exposure construction, decision-process generation, uncertainty-gap selection, rejection sampling and SFT/DPO/GRPO remain unchanged. The pipeline moves from Section 3.3 to Appendix B.2; revised confidence-selection wording does not establish a different procedure.

E1.justification: The same eight recommendation domains, four Amazon subsets and Tulu training mixture remain. Appendix D.6 repartitions existing domains for training and testing without adding represented data coverage or changing the item-selection task.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GPT-5-Nano, GPT-5-Mini, GPT-5.1, Gemini-2.5-Flash and Gemini-3.0-Pro-Preview, substantially broadening comparison beyond open models. GPT-5 also appears in Figure 2 and Table 14. All ten previously evaluated recommendation backbones remain; the reported count changing from eight to ten is a correction.

E3.justification: New protocols include reciprocal training/testing across two domain groups, prediction-entropy comparisons across training stages, and teacher-referenced ROUGE-L, ROUGE-2, BLEU-2 and generation-length evaluation in Appendices D.4–D.6. The original simulation and recommendation evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices D.4–D.6 add substantial analyses of training-stage confidence, reasoning-style transfer and generalization to held-out domains. Appendix F adds movie and music decision-process examples. Existing dataset-size, selection-strategy, factor and feature-ablation analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five sampled outputs per evaluation scene, Table 2's standard deviations and existing plot error bars. New Table 12 supplies additional entropy summaries with undefined ± terms, without documenting a different uncertainty-estimation practice, additional runs, seed policy or significance test.

E6.justification: Existing model rows and recommendation and feature-ablation scores are retained. Substantial new results include Gemini-3.0-Pro-Preview's 47.7% overall accuracy in Table 1 and entropy, style and transfer measurements in Tables 12–14. For example, Table 14 reports Goodreads accuracy of 68.5% with cross-domain training versus 86.9% with full-data training.

T1.justification: Definitions 2.1 and 3.1, Equations 1–3 and Algorithm 1 retain their mathematical content. The new entropy analysis reuses Equation 2; no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory RQ1 shift emphasis from simulating how users think and decide toward aligned actions accompanied by explanatory rationales. The central contributions of feedback-based data construction, lightweight preference alignment and useful recommendation feedback remain.

C2.justification: New interpretations connect lower entropy to more human-like decisions, attribute reasoning structure to SFT and decision refinement to preference optimization, and argue that cross-domain transfer demonstrates generalizable reasoning. Ethical Considerations adds discussion of bias amplification and anonymization. The original multimodal and non-interaction limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds previously missing SASRec/NARM hyperparameters, explains TIME_DIFF formatting and states a constructed-data license. It removes direct dataset/checkpoint links and the disclosure of selection separately by exposure length. The GitHub link, core runtime information and existing training configurations remain; these documentation changes do not establish changed experiments.

R1.justification: v2 trims background citations, including MINDSim, the Qwen2.5 technical report, FPSR+ and several Du et al. recommendation papers. Its positioning as feedback-based fine-tuning complementary to existing agent simulators remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and parts of the introduction, condenses exposure-construction prose and shortens the conclusion. It moves the pipeline description to Appendix B.2 and separates Limitations from Conclusion. Most methodological exposition and the main narrative sequence remain.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, extensively resizing and relocating displays. Tables gain revised grouping and color highlighting; Figure 2 gains a comparator and revised legend/scale. BPR and MultiDAE results move from Table 3 to Table 9, three new tables appear, and appendix figures and prompt boxes are rearranged.

improvement.justification: The stronger external comparisons, held-out-domain evaluation and additional implementation details improve evidence and reproducibility. These gains are tempered by overinterpretation: Appendix D.4 measures entropy without establishing calibration, and D.6 incorrectly claims superiority over GPT-5 on Goodreads despite Table 14 showing 68.5% versus 78.9%. The revision provides a useful but qualified net improvement.
